benchmarks: custom synthetic 5-topic benchmark (own); pilot developer user study (182 organic memories, 20 queries/70 judgments); not evaluated on LoCoMo
fallos_mitigaciones: OWASP ASI06 memory poisoning taxonomy: direct injection, indirect injection, and gradual 'sleeper agent' erosion (S2.1). Mitigated via Bayesian Beta-Binomial trust scoring per agent (Eq.2) with enforcement blocking writes/deletes below trust<0.3 (S4), plus per-memory provenance chain for forensic isolation (S4.2).
cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Memory with Bayesian Trust Defense Against Memory Poisoning.
notes: S3.1-4.2 four-layer local-first stack (SQLite/FTS5+TF-IDF -> hierarchical materialized-path index -> Leiden knowledge-graph clustering -> Beta-Binomial pattern layer) + v2.7 adaptive learning-to-rank re-ranker (9-feature GBDT+LambdaRank) -> operaciones=WRITE(memory writes)+ADMISION(trust<0.3 blocks write/delete)+ACTUALIZACION(Bayesian trust update Eq.2, pattern confidence Eq.1). Table3 layer ablation (1000 memories): base FTS5 MRR=0.90/NDCG@5=0.441; adaptive re-ranker raises NDCG@5 to 0.900 (+104%) confirming mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table4 Bayesian trust defense: benign-vs-malicious trust gap=0.90, sleeper-agent scenario shows 72.4% trust degradation (0.902->0.249) -> strong SEGURIDAD anchor. S5.7 pilot human eval (70 judgments) human MRR=0.70/NDCG@5=0.90. Table1/2 latency+throughput benchmarking (10.6ms median search @100 mems; 220 writes/sec peak @2 agents) -> COSTO. S4.2 provenance fields (created_by/source_protocol/trust_score/provenance_chain) -> FIDELIDAD. Multi-agent coordination via event bus/agent registry, tested up to 10 concurrent agents zero lock errors -> MULTIAGENTE=SI. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD;MULTIAGENTE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) by adding FIDELIDAD (explicit per-memory provenance chain) WRITE COSTO (extensive latency/throughput measurement).

benchmarks: ForgetAgentBench (own, 500 synthetic agent interactions, 1500 labeled deletion targets)
fallos_mitigaciones: Deleted memory can persist/leak via alternative layers (raw text, embeddings, derived-entity summaries, tool transcripts, embedding-neighborhood leakage, LLM context) recoverable via membership-inference, paraphrase retrieval, neighbor leakage, transcript analysis, story-completion attacks (S3/S5). Mitigated via seven-layer deletion pipeline (identify via dependency graph -> raw purge -> embedding tombstone+neighborhood reweighting -> cache/derived-entity invalidation -> transcript sanitization -> cryptographic deletion receipt -> automated red-team verification).
cita: Singhal (2026). ForgetAgent: Verifiable Deletion in Multi-Layer Memory Architectures for LLM Agents.
notes: S3 formal system model M={E,S,C,D,T} (embeddings/structured/caches/derived-entities/tool-transcripts) with (eps,delta)-style counterfactual-indistinguishability deletion security (Eq.def), dependency-closed forget set D_f+ (S3D.3), and lambda-utility-preservation ratio Util=Perf(M',Q_retain)/Perf(M,Q_retain) (S3D.4) -> mide_lectura=SI (utility of retained-memory reads is the explicit evaluation target). S4 seven-layer deletion pipeline = OLVIDO; explicit note that summaries are 'created during memory consolidation' (S3C item3) -> CONSOLIDACION. S7 headline empirical result (abstract, matches Section7): naive deletion 18% robustness vs full layered method 94% robustness with 97% retained task utility on ForgetAgentBench (500 interactions/1500 deletion targets); 5 deletion strategies compared. S3B multi-agent threat actor ('compromised agent': full read/write access to M) + S3C4 'verifiability under multi-agent inference... deleted information reconstructed through cross-agent communication' -> MULTIAGENTE=SI. Cryptographic deletion receipts + declared dependency policy = provenance/verification of deletion state -> FIDELIDAD=SI. F differs from F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;SEGURIDAD) by adding FIDELIDAD (deletion receipts/dependency-policy attestation), MULTIAGENTE (S3C.4 cross-agent threat), RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (utility-preservation metric IS a read-quality measure).

benchmarks: China Mobile 'Lingxi' assistant production logs (own internal benchmark; vertical=443,902 records single-province + horizontal=433,686 records 31-province, sampled from 3.36M raw interactions) + NVIDIA Aegis-1.0 (1000 dangerous-content records, 13 safety categories)
fallos_mitigaciones: Indiscriminate retention creates attack surface for stored credentials/sensitive data and memory-poisoning manipulation (S1 point4), plus privacy/GDPR right-to-be-forgotten conflicts (S1 point5) and quality decay from redundant/obsolete content (S1 points2-3). Mitigated by security-triggered active deletion (safety-risk classification tier) achieving 100% elimination of dangerous content (Table2/3) while retaining >70% high-value business content.
cita: Gu et al. (2026). FSFM: A Biologically-Inspired Framework for Selective Forgetting of Agent Memory.
notes: S3.1 3-layer cognitive architecture (Sensory->Working[7+-2 items, task-completion-triggered clearing]->Long-Term[continuous importance-score pruning]) + S2.1-2.2 Ebbinghaus exponential decay Retention(t)=e^(-lambda t) plus multi-factor probabilistic retention model + RL-framed forgetting-policy optimization -> OLVIDO=core mechanism; task-completion clearing/consolidation into long-term = CONSOLIDACION; capacity-constraint pruning = PRESUPUESTO trigger; retrieval-triggered reconsolidation updates importance scores = ACTUALIZACION. S4.2 ImportanceScoringEngine scores stored as vector-DB metadata (S2.3.1) -> representacion=VECTOR. S4/Table2-3 (10 experimental runs, FSFM vs traditional Baseline) headline results (scale-invariant across both datasets): 30% memory-efficiency gain, 1.3x retrieval speedup, 100% dangerous-content elimination, >70% high-value-content retention, +29.2% content signal-to-noise ratio (abstract) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO/COSTO. S1 point3 'Information Obsolescence' explicitly addresses dynamically updating outdated/stale content -> FIDELIDAD=SI. S1.2/2.4.3 'multi-agent collaboration' listed as application scenario + social_consensus reinforcement signal drawn from 'other agents' (S2.1.2.4) -> MULTIAGENTE=SI. F differs from F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;SEGURIDAD) by adding RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO COSTO FIDELIDAD MULTIAGENTE per above anchors.

benchmarks: custom Trojan Hippo benchmark (OpenEvolve-based adaptive red-teaming, simulated email-assistant scenario; benign multi-session data generated via a modified LoCoMo data-generation pipeline); evaluated against gemini-3.1-pro and gpt-5-mini across 4 memory backends (explicit tool memory, mem0 agentic memory, RAG, sliding-window context)
fallos_mitigaciones: Trojan Hippo: attacker plants a dormant payload via a single untrusted tool call (e.g. crafted email) that is silently written into long-term memory and activates only when the user later discusses sensitive topics (finance/health/legal/tax/identity), exfiltrating data (S3, Fig.2); persists across 100+ benign sessions, up to 85-100% ASR undefended (Fig.1). Mitigated via four memory-system defenses (write-time/retrieval-time/session-boundary controls) reducing ASR to 0-5% in most configs (one defense reaches 0% in all cases), at a quantified security-utility cost (S6-7).
cita: Das et al. (2026). Trojan Hippo: Weaponizing Agent Memory for Data Exfiltration.
notes: S3 two-stage attack: Stage1 Injection (payload from untrusted tool-read content silently WRITTEN to long-term memory, no admission gate catches it undefended) + Stage2 Activation (LLM discretionarily decides to invoke send_email upon recognizing a sensitive-topic trigger embedded in the payload instructions) -> trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM. Fig.1/abstract: undefended ASR up to 100%(gemini-3.1-pro)/85%(gpt-5-mini) across 4 backends (explicit/mem0/RAG/context); defenses cut ASR to 0-5% (one to 0% in all cases) 'at utility costs that vary widely' -> first capability-aware security/utility tradeoff analysis for persistent memory (S6-7) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO/mide_lectura=SI. Explicit trust hierarchy (trusted user/agent vs untrusted external content) is the paper's central provenance distinction that defenses must enforce -> FIDELIDAD=SI. Core contribution IS negative evidence that persistent memory strictly expands the attack surface of even frontier safety-aligned models -> NEGATIVO(b). No multi-agent architecture (single email-assistant agent) -> multiagente=NO. Poisoned content (the payload) persists as raw stored content across an arbitrary number of future sessions until removed -> handoff=CONTENIDO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Static coarse-grained guardrails cause severe over-refusal of benign complex workflows (rigid global margin fails to separate ambiguous benign vs malicious intent, Fig.1a). Mitigated by per-leaf dual-policy rule pairs (prohibition + a synthesized benign exemption) so instructions near a harmful centroid are protected from misclassification by the paired exemption (S3.2 Eq.7); ablation (Table3) shows raw trajectories w/o attack-enhancement raise benign refusal to 25.0% and a flattened (non-hierarchical) rule structure drops harmful refusal to 48.9%, confirming both components are load-bearing.
cita: Liu et al. (2026). SafeHarbor: Defining Precise Decision Boundaries via Hierarchical Memory-Augmented Guardrail for LLM Agent Safety.
notes: NOTE: this is memory-USED-FOR-agent-safety (a guardrail), not security-OF-the-memory-store itself (rule 7, P8) -> SEGURIDAD deliberately EXCLUDED from confirmed F despite F_screening=SEGURIDAD;CONSOLIDACION. S3.3-3.4 offline adversarial rule generator (Goal Decomposition/Privilege Escalation/Contextual Reframing mutations) writes prohibition+exemption pairs into a self-organizing hierarchical memory tree (S3.2, Algorithm1): Shannon-entropy Information-Gain decides new-cluster vs new-leaf vs Merge-and-refine (ADMISION+CONSOLIDACION+ACTUALIZACION); trigger is a mix of LLM-judged informational value ('LLM functions as a strategic attacker... select the optimal attack paradigm', DISCRECIONAL-LLM) and a deterministic Info-Gain threshold tau_gain (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). S3.5 centroid-based top-k cluster retrieval + fast-path/LLM-judgment gating = EMBEDDINGS+RANKING. Table1 headline: peak benign utility 63.6% on GPT-4o, harmful refusal rate >93% (abstract); Table2 AgentSafetyBench: surpasses A-Mem by 14.7% (GPT-4o) and RAG by 16.0% (Qwen2.5-7B) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO/mide_lectura=SI (hierarchical-retrieval structure IS ablated in Table3, directly tying retrieval quality to outcome). Table3 ablation: w/o attack-enhancement benign-refusal->25.0%; flattened rule hierarchy -> harmful-refusal drops to 48.9%. Rules are procedural safety policy (prohibition/exemption pairs governing agent action), not factual/episodic content -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL.

benchmarks: MemPrivacy-Bench (own, 200 synthetic user profiles from PersonaHub seeds, 155k+ privacy instances, 7 scenario categories/23 subcategories); evaluated against GPT-5.2, Gemini-3.1-Pro and multiple cloud memory systems (e.g. Mem0, LongMem)
fallos_mitigaciones: Cloud-assisted memory management exposes PII (contact/health/financial/credentials) to cloud logs/vector DBs/external stores; prior work cites up to 69% multi-turn memory-attack success and 75% leakage-attack success against memory systems (S1). Full masking prevents exposure but destroys task-relevant semantics (benign refusal / broken drafts, Fig.1). MemPrivacy mitigates via a four-level (PL1-PL4) privacy taxonomy + local edge-side detection replacing sensitive spans with type-aware placeholders before cloud transmission, restoring original values locally (utility loss held within 1.6% across memory systems).
cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemPrivacy: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Memory Management for Edge-Cloud Agents.
notes: S3 formal problem def: local sanitization Fsan produces Xsafe (typed placeholders e.g. <Health_Info_1>) sent to cloud memory/agent C, local restoration Fres recovers Yhat; objective minimizes privacy-leakage-risk Rpriv s.t. utility-loss Lutil<=eps (Eq.1-5). S4 3-stage lifecycle: Stage1 on-device PL1-PL4 detection+typed-placeholder replacement WRITTEN to a local secure mapping DB (WRITE; PL-tier classification=ADMISION-like gating of what reaches cloud) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (local key-value mapping table), retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS (Stage3 'lightweight database lookup and string substitution'). Fig.2 explicitly labels the mapping DB 'Persistent Across Sessions' (Session A -> <Type_1>, Session B -> <Type_1>) -> only the placeholder/pointer crosses to the cloud/session boundary while the real value stays local -> handoff=PUNTEROS. Abstract headline: MemPrivacy 'substantially surpassing' GPT-5.2/Gemini-3.1-Pro on privacy-span extraction, 'reducing inference latency', and limiting utility loss to within 1.6% across multiple widely-used memory systems (vs baseline masking) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO/mide_lectura=SI (cross-system utility-loss IS the read-quality metric) + COSTO (latency reduction measured). Attack surface being defended is privacy leakage/extraction FROM the memory store itself (not memory-for-security) -> SEGURIDAD retained. No provenance/staleness verification of stored content is discussed (privacy != fidelity) -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Single edge-cloud pipeline per user, no cross-agent sharing -> multiagente=NO.
